verdicts.strongest_argument: This finding is a description of the price bars and the captured wire copy, and its own text says so - 'What is priced, violently, is the buyback and the cash-shell discount.' Every input is published in this corpus and dated before the print. The buyback release is in captured retail wire copy at docs/c64c6b6862121be1edca7d02c3f510e6f2384e9a.txt (item 1 of snapshots/20260907T150856Z.json): the 2026-09-03T10:21 message reads '17 Education & Technology Group Inc. approved a $10 million share repurchase program effective September 3, 2026, to be funded from existing cash. RTPR pushed this release out to users at 6:00:00 AM ET', with the StockTitan URL posted at 10:16 the same morning. The valuation argument is in the same body at 10:33 - 'They have $51M cash and a $24.75M market cap' - and so is the liquidity frame at 22:27 ('20-day average volume is ~7,300 shares. At $2.28 that's about $17K of daily liquidity') and the 7.51m float at 22:02. The prior-year template is in the same body too, at 2025-09-03T21:09: '$10M shares repurchase program'. And the tape has fully executed on it: quote.json goes 2.28 on 09-02 to 2.77 on 09-03 on 2,789,500 shares against a 20-day median of about 4,600, then 2.92 on 09-04 and a partial 3.4502 bar on 09-08 against the baseline's 3.79 close - +93.4% in five sessions on a 600x volume day. The discount-to-net-cash arithmetic the hunter runs is correct (about 51% on 09-03, about 20% by 09-08) but it is arithmetic on two numbers both published in the corpus and a price everyone can see. Nothing here is information the market lacks; the only unpublished element is the structural observation that last year's +19.02% bundled buyback and results while this year splits them six sessions apart, which is drawn from the baseline history and filings.json rather than from any captured commentary.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The strongest possible confirmation, and it is in the capture's own bars: 2026-09-02 close 2.28 on 38,400 shares; 2026-09-03 close 2.77 on 2,789,500 shares; 2026-09-04 2.92; 2026-09-08 partial 3.4502 at 15:08 UTC against the baseline's 3.79 close. run_up_5d +93.37%, run_up_20d +57.92%, realised_vol_20d 142.2%. The baseline's session_conflict block for 2026-09-03 records event_day_volume 2,789,500 against median_20d_before of 4,600. Information that produces a 600x volume day and a 21.5% gap is in the price by definition.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Nothing in this corpus - only a demonstration that the 09-03 to 09-08 move was driven by something other than the buyback and cash discount would reopen it, and the captured feed says the opposite.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Both halves of this are published and both are visible in the bars. The +359% revenue headline is not merely reachable in the 2026-06-17 6-K; it was recirculating on the captured retail feed the evening before this print - docs/9d6fda9a47e9a1e05f7738d51d5c7827d0bacfcc.txt, item 1 of snapshots/20260908T150822Z.json, message timestamped 2026-09-07T21:38: 'Q1 2026 revenue +359% YoY to CNY 99.5M and driven by its AI learning product Yiqi Aixue', tagged Bullish. The same figure is in the older body at 2026-06-17T04:12: 'released its Q1 2026 unaudited results, showing revenue jumping 359% YoY and a narrowed net loss.' And the reaction is directly checkable in the capture's own bars rather than only in the baseline: quote.json closes 2.4000 on 2026-06-16 and 2.2900 on 2026-06-17, which is -4.583% - the baseline's -4.58% to three digits. So a triple-digit growth print being sold is a fact published twice in the corpus and printed in the price bars on the day it happened. The residual value of the claim is not new information but a base-rate reconstruction: separating the three results 6-Ks from the five non-results 6-Ks the text matcher caught. That is legitimate analytical work on a baseline that threw its history away, and I do not dispute it - but a company's own past reaction to its own past release is the market's memory, not something the market has failed to price. The reconstruction also thins out under scrutiny: it yields a sample of three, one of which (2026-03-25, 0.0%) is a zero on 8,500-share liquidity and one of which (2025-09-04, +19.02%) the claim itself sets aside as buyback-paired, leaving a single clean observation to carry the inference.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The capture's bars confirm the reaction independently of the baseline: 2026-06-16 close 2.4000 on 14,900 shares, 2026-06-17 close 2.2900 on 10,400 shares, -4.58%, with no run-up in the preceding week (2.2369 to 2.40 over 06-18 to 06-16). The 2026-05-28 auditor-change 6-K day is also in the bars via the baseline at -3.99%. Against that, the current set-up is not remotely comparable: the same stock is up 93.4% in five sessions into this print on 142% realised vol, so a base rate estimated on 10,000-share days at $2.29 is being applied to a different liquidity and positioning regime.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: If the corpus contained a captured preview treating the +359% growth rate as a reason this print will be rewarded - i.e. evidence the market is anchored the opposite way - the base-rate correction would become genuinely contrarian and drop toward 40.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The claim's own premise - 'nobody sums a Form 4 series, which is exactly why the corpus contains the twelve announcements and no total' - is wrong twice. First as a matter of the form: a Form 4 reports securities beneficially owned following the reported transaction, so the running total is on the face of every individual filing and no summation is required. Second, and decisively for this corpus: the captured ceo-buys.com messages in docs/c64c6b6862121be1edca7d02c3f510e6f2384e9a.txt each carry that running total explicitly - 'Liu Chang now owns 113,070 shares' (2026-09-04T13:45) and 'Liu Chang now owns 35,149 shares' (2026-07-20T12:40). The aggregate the hunter says nobody computes is a one-line subtraction between two numbers published in the same captured feed, and the eleven visible dollar tickets in that feed sum to about $135,000, so the sub-$200k scale is readable off the corpus directly. Every one of the underlying filings is also indexed in filings.json with its accession and date (2026-07-06 through 2026-09-04, thirteen Form 4 accessions, not twelve as the claim states). On magnitude the claim concedes its own case: about $170k against event.json's $24.75m market cap is 0.69%, roughly ten days of the $17k daily dollar liquidity the same feed quotes - immaterial by construction. The bearish tell that remains, 'it stopped on 2026-09-04', has a mundane published-calendar explanation: the results date was announced for September 8 on 2026-09-02 (same body, 18:30), so an insider going quiet in the days before a results release is the ordinary blackout pattern rather than a signal.

prior_publication.what_it_says: The last Form 4 in the series, which by the form's design states total beneficial ownership after the purchase.
Each announcement publishes both the ticket size and the cumulative holding - 35,149 shares on 07-20 rising to 113,070 on 09-04 - so the aggregate stake build is published, not latent.
The results date was public on 2026-09-02, giving the ordinary blackout explanation for purchases ceasing on 09-04.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The bars say the drip was never the driver, which cuts for the hunter's materiality point and against its novelty. Across the whole purchase window 2026-07-20 to 2026-09-01 the stock went 2.08 to 2.08 with volumes between 0 and 68,200 shares, so twelve bullish headlines moved nothing; then the price doubled on the buyback day when the CEO bought $19,819. On a 7.51m float, 78,000 shares is about 1%, and at 0.69% of market cap it sits far inside the 2.15% deadband the baseline sets.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence that the twelve tickets were part of a coordinated stake build large enough to matter - a 13D or a change-of-control filing tied to Liu Chang rather than to the existing holders - would make the aggregate meaningful and drop this below 40.

interactions: YQ#0 and YQ#2 rest on the same stored body, docs/c64c6b6862121be1edca7d02c3f510e6f2384e9a.txt, which the hunter declares; that single document supplies the buyback text, the $51m-cash-versus-$24.75m-cap line, the float, the $17k liquidity figure and all eleven insider tickets, so four of the six sourced numbers across this brief trace to one stocktwits dump fetched 2026-09-07. YQ#0 and YQ#1 also point in the same direction by opposite routes - #0 says the catalyst is spent, #1 says growth headlines get sold here - and both would be double-counting the same bearish read on the same six sessions. Separately, filings.json carries a SCHEDULE 13D/A filed 2026-09-08 (accession 0001193125-26-384376), one session before the print and inside the squeeze, which no finding in this brief addresses.
corpus_limits: The YQ capture stored two bodies, both stocktwits dumps, and no company release, no 6-K text and no news article, so I could not read the buyback release, the results-date release or any results 6-K directly - every company fact here reaches me through a retail feed quoting it. I could not verify the $51m cash figure or whether it is gross or net of liabilities, nor the share count behind the $24.75m and roughly $41m market-cap figures, since no 20-F or 6-K body is stored (the 20-F, accession 0001193125-26-191472 of 2026-04-29, is indexed but not captured). quote.json's final bar for 2026-09-08 is partial (3.4502 at 15:08 UTC, 162,595 shares) so I used the baseline's 3.79 close for the run-in, and no 2026-09-09 bar exists in the capture or was used. The three prior reactions the base-rate claim relies on (2025-09-04, 2026-03-25, 2026-06-17) are only partly checkable in the bars, which begin 2026-06-09; only the 2026-06-17 figure could be recomputed. No option chain, no implied move, no skew. No document in this capture carried tripwire_tells.
